chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
About a man who sets out on a journey, then it occurs to him to stay while he is in salat (prayer). He said: “He completes [the prayer] when the decision to stay becomes apparent to him.”
And about a man who accompanies his brother to the place where shortening the prayer and breaking the fast become obligatory upon him. He said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the prayer due to travel
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel that brings the rulings of shortening prayer and breaking the fast
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being performed at the time of the change in intention
key_terms.الْإِفْطَارُ: breaking the fast due to the legal concession of travel
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: residing or deciding to stay in a place rather than continue travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he completes the prayer in full rather than shortening it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler decides to reside while in the middle of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings related to travel, salat (prayer), and fasting. It states that if a traveler decides to reside while in prayer, he completes the prayer in full, and it also permits accompanying another person to the point where the rulings of travel begin.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1298 - Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu al-Hasan (as)

about a man who sets out on a journey and then decides to stay (reside) while he is in the midst of prayer.
Imam (as) said: "He should complete (the full prayer) when he decides to stay."

He also asked about a man who accompanies his brother to the point where shortening prayers and breaking the fast becomes obligatory.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
